title: Distribute Elements Into Two Arrays I
summary: Given a 1-indexed array of distinct integers, distribute its elements into two arrays, arr1 and arr2, through n operations.
statement: Given a 1-indexed array of distinct integers, distribute its elements into two arrays, arr1 and arr2, through n operations. Start by appending the first element to arr1 and the second to arr2. For each subsequent element, append it to arr1 if its last element is greater than arr2's last element, or to arr2 otherwise. The final result is the concatenation of arr1 and arr2.
constraints: Start result1 with nums[0] and result2 with nums[1].
For each later value, append it to result1 when result1’s last value is greater than result2’s last value; otherwise append to result2.
hints: The rule depends only on the two current last elements.
Maintain the two result arrays directly.
Compare their tails for each next value and append to the selected array.
This mirrors every deterministic distribution step, and the final concatenation follows the required order.
